; Render transient effects, level records and secondary records in that order. This renderer is duplicated in four physical level banks; CPU aliases do not identify the copy.
; Scan 16 records backwards. Bit $20 enables rendering; subtract the 16-bit camera position from planar X/Y fields. The low type nibble selects the clipped vertical-chain draw consumer.
; Save the record index because the draw consumer can clobber X.
; Continue with the preceding record; negative X terminates the scan.
; Draw the level record as a clipped vertical chain. Bias X by 64; the low type nibble determines the number of eight-pixel rows and whether the first row uses the alternate template pair.
; Advance projected Y by eight, reject offscreen high bytes and rows below 167, then append the selected component. Decrease the remaining type count by two per row.

; Level-column component template: attribute/tile pairs indexed from Y=5 or 7. AppendTemplateSprite increments Y before each byte, so preserve the original cursor bias. Exact component selection follows the packed record type.
; Scan the second 16-record array. Bit $02 marks visible records; convert its fifth plane to an eightfold index minus one before drawing. The quad draw body uses four clipped template components.
; Project the next secondary record into camera-relative coordinates.
; Restore the saved record index and continue backwards.
; Project four template components using local X/Y biases. Skip clipped components; the record's frame selector biases the paired template index.
; Two four-byte coordinate-bias columns, X then Y, indexed 3 down to 0 by DrawSecondaryQuad. These project the four template components; bytes retain their unsigned addition/carry behavior.

; Secondary draw attribute/tile pairs selected with twice the component index plus the record frame bias. Nearby repeated template content is non-code; the exact original grouping of the whole span remains unresolved.
; Scan 16 effect slots. A negative type disables a slot; discard coordinates with nonzero camera-relative high bytes, then choose a draw path by effect type.
; Preserve the slot while helpers use X for table indexing.
; Skip disabled, clipped or unsupported effect states.
; Use the projected origin only above the lower clipping boundary. State 0 uses a lookup; state 2 selects a paired frame directly, while state 1 is skipped.
; Translate the effect frame through the local lookup, double it, and bias the draw index by minus one.
; Choose the paired frame index for this effect; zero state takes the alternate fixed-index path.
; Use the zero-state draw index, biased by $13.
; State 4 uses the effect frame; other states take the shared fixed-index path. Exact visual meanings remain unresolved.
; Use the alternate fixed draw index; The shared component writer appends the selected sprite to OAM.
; Eight effect-frame remap values, consumed before doubling and biasing the component cursor. The table is bounded by the adjoining template data and renderer code.
; Effect attribute/tile pairs read through the sprite-frame pointer and selected by the effect state/frame paths. The common writer starts immediately after this data at 9E84.
; Read attribute/tile bytes after template cursor Y, combine flip bits, and append Y/tile/attribute/X to shadow OAM. Update the byte cursor and sprite count; temporary pushes preserve byte order.
; Small renderer flip/index constants bracketed by the component writer and occlusion routine. Exact original table grouping is unresolved; no instruction role is inferred.

; When occlusion is enabled, preserve X and quantize sprite coordinates plus scroll into the 0600 visibility grid. FF returns normally; another cell value discards one caller return address. No natural caller is established.
; Restore X, discard the immediate caller's return address, and return to its caller. This is a nonlocal draw abort, not a normal fallthrough.
; Sixteen quantized row/nametable offsets. The occlusion helper adds a masked vertical cell offset to this horizontal-index result before reading the 0600 visibility grid.

; Map the current level resource bank into slot 8000 and copy 32 bytes from the stage palette pointer into the palette shadow. Slot A000 remains bank 13.
; Subtract one brightness band from all 32 palette-shadow bytes; replace underflow with black.
; Use the active actor index minus three to check a pending flag, select its animation delay and clear the flag. The table's exact game meaning remains unresolved.
; Probe terrain below the actor and retire it on contact. Otherwise advance Y by two or three according to its animation frame, retaining carry into the high coordinate.
; Clear the active slot and actor flags and move the actor's X high byte out of the active world window.

; For the selected route actor, consume the per-tick latch and decrement its signed route distance. At expiry, run the optional transition, decode the next route record and initialize its behavior; still perform player contact testing.
; Resolve actor from current active slot, test ground/material and compare its 16-bit X against a stored reference. Facing selects a left/right probe; dispatch effects when the probe accepts.
; Skip a redundant probe for facing 4; otherwise sample $14 pixels left and return if blocked.
; Set the actor-relative marker once if the earlier probe fails.
; Move the selected actor down two pixels and restart its animation at frame one with delay four.
; A pending actor transition selects a spawn helper and then applies the decoded route action. Preserve route/active-slot indices across the local effect update.
; Project active slot to actor index. State 1 advances a 32-step vertical-motion table, while later states clear a per-actor motion field. Actor facing and collision probes constrain movement.
; Index signed vertical steps by the actor's phase, add the 16-bit displacement and advance the bounded phase toward 32.
; At a short remaining delay clear the actor-relative motion phase, then continue the route action through the common dispatcher.
; Add or subtract the actor's stored step from its 16-bit X according to facing four. Both carry and borrow update the high coordinate before terrain checks.
; After motion step 16 optionally spawn an effect and clear its flag. Probe ground and special material; successful contact switches active-slot animation state to 2.
; At frame three with less than two delay ticks, deactivate the slot, reset its state and move it outside the active X window. Continue contact checking on other ticks.
; At the last delay tick of frame three, clear the slot and retire actor 1C. The exact visual effect represented by this reserved actor is unresolved.
; Same reserved-actor retirement contract, triggered at frame two instead of three.
; Search active slots 7 through 1 for actor index 1C and clear the matching slot. Return immediately after the first match.

; Tick palette animation, set effect-active flag from its remaining resource, and derive an area origin relative to the player. On a timed pulse scan eligible active actors and dispatch the type-dependent consumer.
; Store player position minus $0180 in both axes and decrement remaining resource at $32-tick intervals.
; Continue scanning actor indices down to one. The matched handler performs the type-specific area effect and HUD marker update; maintain the saved scan index across calls.
; Small lookup bytes adjoining the HUD marker/update worker. Local consumers and non-instruction patterns were checked; precise field/group meaning remains unresolved.
; Find the HUD OAM tile 34, replace it with tile 36 and position it from the current coarse actor offsets. Preserve caller X/Y around the sound request.
; Every three countdown ticks advance a 13-phase index and alternate palette bytes $34/$35 at four-byte intervals.
; Write the alternate color for this pulse, then advance to the preceding palette entry.

; Subtract the reference origin and quantize both coordinates into 32-pixel cells. Reject cells outside the interior window, fold each axis around the center and use the resulting local table index. Carry set returns a valid lookup byte; clear rejects.
; Thirteen row-base values used after folding relative actor coordinates around the lookup center. Add the folded Y index to form the fixed-table lookup index.
; Process pickup/refill selection, health refill, weapon drain and timed-area effect in sequence.
; Drain the shared meter conditionally: selected weapon 8 can sustain it while fire is held; other cases drain on a four-tick countdown. Clear firing latch at zero.
; Drain pending pickup work first. Select changes weapon only when the debounce expires and direction/fire bits are clear; format the chosen resource as decimal HUD digits.
; Cycle nine selectors, skipping unavailable mask bits and empty resource pools. Commit a changed selection and restart debounce.
; While the pickup display timer is active, add bounded resource units on queued refill ticks and update decimal HUD output. Pickup type maps through a separate selector table.
; Increment health up to $18 while refill work remains, consuming a countdown and clearing its request at completion.
; Scan 32 actors. Cull off-camera ordinary actors while preserving special types; bind eligible visible actors to one of eight active animation slots and initialize their animation/render pointers.
; Use 16-bit differences and margin windows rather than only low bytes. Actor zero and special actor types have different removal rules.
; Search an inactive slot. Mark the actor when capacity is unavailable; otherwise install actor index, facing, initial state and delay.
; Initialize the actor-to-active-slot binding and both frame-pointer buffers under the copy-ready flag.
; Scan 16 planar level records and set/clear bit $20 from camera-relative X/Y with a vertical cutoff. Disabled records keep their existing state.
; Clear visibility for low Y >=$AA; otherwise return to the visible case.

; Skip disabled records and unsupported categories. A shared timer gates decrementing or incrementing the low type nibble according to direction bit 10, preserving upper flags and issuing endpoint sounds.
; Toggle direction bit 10, force the low state active and set the short two-tick update delay.
; Toggle direction and decrement the packed record state, then set the eight-tick delay.

; Search enabled, nonnegative level records in reverse order. Require terminal low state, an accepted coordinate probe and one of two narrow horizontal contact windows; carry clear returns the selected record index.
; Compare actor X/Y to planar record Y. Return carry clear inside the narrow vertical interval and carry set outside; preserve low coordinate differences in shared scratch.
; Search eligible level records backwards. Type >=3, coordinate window and actor facing choose contact side. Carry clear reports a selected contact with A as side; carry set means none.
; Alternate entry to the level-record search with facing already supplied in 0714. Reset the result latch, scan sixteen records backwards and return side/contact with carry clear.
; Preserve the active slot index while starting record expansion or contraction according to its current low nibble. Clear the selected-record latch.
; Camera-relative culling for the second planar record array. Bit 0 disables and bit 1 records visibility; high-byte and lower-screen bounds reject offscreen entries.
; Clear visibility at Y >=$AA; restore the scan index through the loop.
; Map active slot to actor, then test visible enabled secondary records through the bounded world-coordinate window helper. Carry clear returns the selected record index.
; Restore current active slot after scanning and return carry set when no handler accepted.
; Compare actor X against a secondary record within 18 pixels, and its Y against the eight-pixel support window. Carry set rejects; clear reports contact.
; On accepted contact, read the record payload, mark its slot collected, add ten score units, request pickup audio and invoke the common collection continuation.
; Start the pickup display timer. Selector chooses a refill amount, resource unlock bits or health-refill work; an existing pickup is routed to the pending queue instead.
; Convert unsigned A into hundreds/tens/units by repeated subtraction, then add into six unpacked decimal score digits with carry. The decimal digits are binary bytes, not packed BCD.
; Two cascaded countdowns decrement health at zero, clamped against negative wrap. The adjacent four-digit countdown borrows according to a radix table and clears all digits when exhausted.
; Subtract through four digit positions with table-defined reload values; zero is the terminal display.
; Return after a successful decrement or terminal clear.
; Generic non-code at these physical bounds. Nearby code, references and byte patterns were checked in the saved structural review; the precise consumer and internal record schema remain unresolved.
; Convert two values into three eight-unit meter segments using a tile table.
; Weapon meter units are consumed eight at a time; use a partial-segment table for the final remainder and empty tiles thereafter.
; Write a full meter segment while preserving remaining units on the stack; then restore the remainder and advance the bounded segment loop.
; Fill the remaining segment positions with the empty tile.
; Generic non-code at these physical bounds. Nearby code, references and byte patterns were checked in the saved structural review; the precise consumer and internal record schema remain unresolved.
; Render health in three eight-unit segments, sharing positions and partial-tile table with the other meter.
; Write full health segments, then loop with the remaining units; empty trailing segments use tile $34.
; Clear a PPU span, copy the fixed HUD tile strip, then write stage-dependent attribute bytes. Requires display-safe PPU access and bank 13 in slot A000.

; Start enters pause only when no fade is active. Dim palette, wait for Start release and debounce, process the ten-step pause shortcut, then require Start press/release before resuming and restoring palette.

; Compare each released controller state to the ten-byte shortcut. Matching steps require a five-tick hold/release boundary. Complete match clears pause, fades out and enters the transition tail; mismatch resets progress.
; Disable display and IRQ, clear runtime objects, increment the stage and remove two return addresses before restarting at the fixed stage entry. This bypasses the ordinary completion test.
; A mismatched shortcut input restarts at index zero.

; Ten controller-state bytes consumed by the pause shortcut comparator. Each accepted step requires release before advancing; complete sequence enters the level transition. See scenarios.json for the tested input recipe.
; Clear shadow OAM/work spans, level and secondary record flags, and the player slot before a transition.

; Unless the player is in terminal state $1D, update survival/time counters and blink flag. Decrement bounded per-effect/cooldown timers, then process the gameplay palette fade under the selected level bank.
; Fade state 1/2 activates direction and initial step; five-tick intervals adjust 32 source palette colors, clamping dark values to black.
; Generic non-code at these physical bounds. Nearby code, references and byte patterns were checked in the saved structural review; the precise consumer and internal record schema remain unresolved.

; Return to the effect dispatcher after the preceding selected behavior finishes. This accepted one-byte continuation retains its caller context; it is not evidence for unrelated isolated return bytes.

; Gate ordinary actors by proximity and type/state. Some actors move four pixels according to facing before the shared terrain collision helper; inactive actors can be reactivated by their record field.
; Subtract four from actor X with high-byte borrow, then run the shared terrain movement helper.
; Read planar record field $A0 and require its proximity test before setting actor-active bit.
; Probe the effect at X plus four at two vertical sample points eight pixels apart, then resolve its tile/material response through the common bank-restoring helper.
; Alternate entry to the two-height effect probe. Build X plus four and Y plus eight from the effect, resolve the world cell and tail-call the bank-restoring material response.
; Choose X plus six or the raw X according to effect direction, add four to Y and probe the resulting world cell.
; Probe at effect X plus four and its unmodified Y, then restore the level resource bank through the shared material helper.

; Build a 24 by 24 box around the effect. Map frame bank 12 to build active actor rectangles, restore the level bank before damage dispatch, and stop at an accepted target. Restore mapping on the no-hit exit too.

; For the supported player attack states, build a facing-dependent 32 by 16 box beside the player. Scan active actor rectangles with bank 12 temporarily mapped and tail-dispatch accepted attack damage after restoring the level bank.
; Near frame end copy slot facing into actor facing. Test player collision, resolve vertical terrain motion and retain the resulting direction in the active slot.
; Probe above or below from the current direction. On success, move the actor four pixels and set direction 1 or 3; an obstructed probe discards one caller return address.
; Discard the immediate caller return address so an obstructed vertical motion skips its remaining behavior.
; For an active actor, test the taller packed proximity bound and invoke the existing frame/contact continuation when accepted.
; Only state-zero actors move. Apply a two-pixel Y step in the selected direction, then use the shared four-pixel terrain correction/direction helper.
; Use the taller actor's stage record to choose its proximity activation and terrain/contact continuation.
; Unless excluded by player state/frame, adjust player Y at an eight-pixel boundary and align its low nibble to A. This is geometric alignment; the support object's visual name remains unresolved.
; Test secondary records for player slot zero; invoke follow-up only if the collision result accepts it. Pending pickup types are stored by the adjacent helper.
; Store the new pickup type at the current queue index, increment the queue cursor and return.
; Pop the latest queued pickup selector. Discard the caller return address before tail-jumping to pickup application; this deliberate nonlocal return matters to callers.
; Near frame end synchronize facing, then perform player damage/contact tests and terrain movement; store the resulting direction.
; Near animation end choose the left/right terrain correction from slot facing, write the resulting direction, and reset actor state/frame to zero.

; If reserved actor 1B is free, initialize it beside the selected actor using facing-dependent X plus/minus 16 and Y minus four. Reset the attachment state; its exact visual identity remains unresolved.
; Move player Y upward one pixel; once the animation has advanced from frame zero, enter the shared recovery state.
; At a narrow frame-delay window, require player hit eligibility and a close actor/player distance. Enter player state 1E and reset its frame/delay, with a short motion timer.
; When neither fade nor pause is active, selected stages rotate three palette colors every fourth timer interval.
; Use stage-indexed 16-bit target coordinates. If player X/Y are each within a $20-wide unsigned window, enter the ordinary completion tail; otherwise return.
; Generic non-code at these physical bounds. Nearby code, references and byte patterns were checked in the saved structural review; the precise consumer and internal record schema remain unresolved.

; Only at eight-pixel Y alignment, sample terrain on both sides of the player. Two signed material results select displacement direction/state or adjust X by four before switching falling states. Material meanings remain tentative.
; Sample player X minus four; shared routine probes Y plus $10 and derives a material response from mask/bit tests.
; Sample player X plus four through the same material classifier.
; Convert world coordinates to a banked map pointer, read tile material and test subcell mask. Return 0 for no effect, 1 or $FF for opposite responses selected by a second table.
; Expand each saved origin by a margin and compare 16-bit X/Y differences against combined extents. Carry set means overlap; clear means separated.
; Move player down six pixels and eight horizontally according to facing; shared by support/contact transitions.
; Sample player Y minus ten and delegate low tile types to the fixed collision-mask helper. Other types return carry clear.

; Update facing from left/right input. While fire is held, pace resource consumption and audio by the action cooldown; exhausted/released fire enters a recovery animation. Active fire tests the player attack box.
; Allocate an effect or nonlocally abort on exhaustion. Initialize its lifetime/type, choose direction and launch offsets from player state/facing, then request firing audio.
; Two signed little-endian launch-offset columns: X at BCBD and Y at BCC5. Facing and player aiming state select the doubled entry index.
; Set effect type one, state zero and lifetime one. Convert player facing into a compact direction index and return its doubled table index in X.

; Require cooldown zero and a nonzero resource. Allocate and position the simple effect at a facing-dependent X and state-dependent Y offset, consume one unit and request sound. Empty stock imposes a longer retry delay.

; Require action cooldown zero and dispatch the selected weapon: one path checks its stock and spawns a directed effect, another enters player state 20, and selector two uses pool 074C. Exact original weapon names remain tentative.
; Update facing and require down plus fire to sustain the action. Pace resource use and the attack box; releasing inputs selects recovery or idle.
; Restore the level bank and load up to two route stream pointers from stage-specific fixed tables. Decode the first record of each nonnull stream.
; A selects one of two streams and Y its byte cursor. Negative first byte wraps to the stream start; read action, transition flag and a little-endian target/distance word, then save the next cursor.
; Map the decoded action to idle/moving/turning behavior, reset frame/delay and initialize facing and quantized route distance as required.
; Compare the route target word with actor X and set facing left or right in both actor and slot state.
; Compute facing-dependent unsigned horizontal distance to the route target, divide by 32 and store its coarse route count.
; Search five effect actor slots for inactive entries. Copy facing and spawn offset X +/-12 and Y minus eight, reset state and set pending flag. Full allocation failure queues audio $24.
; Complete the right-facing spawn coordinate with carry, then initialize Y/state/flag and continue scanning.
; Ignore terminal state three. Subtract the selected effect's damage from the actor health byte; borrow triggers the fixed defeat/reward helper. Carry set reports an accepted hit.
; Ignore terminal state three, otherwise subtract one health unit and invoke the defeat/reward helper on borrow. Carry set reports acceptance.
; Uniform $00 bytes; retained as generic non-code after boundary and code-conflict review. Original fill/allocation purpose is unknown.
; Map physical PRG pair 8/9 through the supported mapper helper and jump to its CPU $8000 entry.

Signed motion columns C08A/C0B4/C0FC and launch/facing tables C146..C1B8 serve player/effect/contact routines. C1C4 contains subcell masks. These are consumer origins, not a claim that every intervening byte has a recovered schema; retain unresolved repeated constants as generic non-code.
; Sample actor origin and three adjacent map bytes. Switch from map bank to material bank, compare sentinels and return carry according to the center/flanking combination.
; Add A to actor X, use actor Y plus ProbeYOffset, translate world coordinates and test material. Carry result comes from the fixed mask consumer for tile types below $0E.
; Store 16-bit actor Y plus ProbeYOffset into probe-coordinate scratch.
; Subtract A from actor X using incoming carry, then share the right-probe map/material path. Callers must establish the subtraction carry contract.
; Copy actor X to shared 16-bit probe scratch.
; Set X to actor origin, Y plus $10, then scan an $FF-terminated special-tile list. Carry clear means tile appears in the list; carry set means absent.
; World/map translation precedes an $FF-sentinel list lookup in the level-resource bank.

; Require X on the appropriate half-cell, sample the world 32 pixels above the actor and search the FF-terminated special-tile list. Carry clear reports a matching tile; restore the level resource bank before the list read.
; Sample 22 pixels above actor X, resolve the world tile and map it through the material table. FF rejects with carry set; other material values return carry clear.
; Apply the caller's vertical offset, resolve the world tile and material, and report FF as carry set. Restore the level bank before consuming material data.
; Subtract the supplied X offset and enter the common horizontal material probe. Y and the carry convention come from that shared consumer.
; Sample actor X plus scratch offset and its Y origin. $FF is solid; packed $33/$CC masks select a horizontal half-cell based on world X bit $10. Return carry as collision result.
; Add A to actor Y and store the 16-bit result; shared by collision probes.
; Use actor X plus eight with caller-provided Y offset, then enter material-mask sampling.
; Apply the caller's vertical offset and sample eight pixels left before joining the common probe. This is an accepted entry, not the earlier unresolved placeholder.
; Use actor origin and A as Y offset, resolve banked map byte and material mask, then choose one of eight subcell bits from X bit 4 and vertical low bits. Carry set denotes collision.

; Seven sixteen-byte subcell collision masks. The material record supplies a three-bit mask selector; the probe combines masked X/Y subcells, optionally mirrors the column with bit 80, and reports a nonzero mask cell as contact.
; Resolve the player's sample tile, search paired tile/mask records, form a 4 by 4 subcell index and mirror its column when bit 80 is set. A nonzero fixed mask reports carry set.
; Search the FF-terminated special tile list, constrain subcell position and read the neighboring byte in the map bank. Restore level mapping before returning the final material decision.
; Read the sampled map tile, restore level mapping, translate through tile type then fixed collision-mask tables. Nonzero collision reports carry set.
; Probe player Y+$10, scan tile/value pairs until $FF and apply an additional vertical-half check when the paired flag is nonzero.
; Scan actors 31 down to one whose flags 0E are clear. Actor type selects one of fifteen bounded initializer entries; their static handler contracts are established independently of pointer values.
; Index the banked word table by twice actor type; tail-jump through the resulting pointer. A pointer alone is not code evidence for other entries.
; Scan slots 7..1, calling the animation/state update for active slots.
; Map bank 12, resolve frame/state tables and save the next frame pointer; restore the level resource bank, then dispatch behavior by type and state.
; Write the resolved frame pointer to the pending buffer with copy-ready flag cleared; set it after both bytes are written for NMI copying.
; Actor type selects a state table; actor state selects a frame sequence; active-slot frame index selects the current frame record.
; Decrement delay, advance frame on underflow and recognize a $FFFF pair as state-transition marker followed by replacement actor state. Load the next frame's delay byte.

; Resolve type/state through a second nested pointer table and tail-jump to the selected behavior. All fifteen actor-type domains have matched frame and behavior state counts; natural selection of individual states remains separate.
; Copy facing near the end of a frame, then call actor/player collision and terrain movement helpers.
; Near frame end copy facing; test player overlap, additional contact constraints and terrain movement.
; Near animation end, require an eligible player state and close distance window. Reset the actor to state two/frame zero/delay five when accepted.
; Check contact, synchronize facing near frame end, move against terrain and retain the result. Reset actor state and animation frame for the next behavior.
; Use relative position to choose a close-range state-five animation or reverse direction through the shared facing helper.
; Until frame three, move actor downward two pixels and probe support. Contact aligns Y, enters the terminal frame/delay and plays landing audio; terminal frames use player contact testing.
; Lookup by player state; require a nonzero entry and no blink timer. Carry set means player hit tests are enabled.
; Respect hit enable and optional per-slot emitted-sprite count. Map frame bank for both collision rectangles, restore level bank and test overlap; accepted collision delegates damage behavior.
; Tail-call the common saturating health subtraction with damage two.
; Mark contact, request hit audio and choose reaction by player eligibility state and relative facing. Reset animation and delay, with special-mode and airborne recovery alternatives.
; Gate contact through player-hit eligibility, active actors and relative position/facing windows; accepted terrain contact can invoke additional behavior.

; On an accepted relative-position window, reset actor frame/state and discard caller return addresses. Actor type 0C creates the reserved side attachment and uses a longer delay. These are intentional nonlocal exits.
; Search active slots 7..1 for actor type 7 or type 2 in an early state. Carry set reports a blocker.
; Search active slots for actor type five in state three or above. Carry set reports a blocker; clear means none found.

; Choose directional ground/side probes from facing; accepted movement can unwind the caller return with PLA/PLA/RTS. Otherwise invoke alternate actor behavior or contact continuation. Do not treat these as ordinary local returns.
; Discard one caller return address before returning from terrain rejection.
; Set actor Y for the right-side movement response; accepted support returns without correction, while obstruction can shift the actor or abort the caller.
; Set actor facing four and return after the terrain response.
; Subtract eight from the actor's 16-bit X coordinate.
; Apply the mirrored side probe, then combine support/material/ground checks through the common left-terrain response.
; Combine side, support, material and ground probes. Keep the current motion when accepted; otherwise shift right and face right through the shared correction.
; Move actor right eight pixels and set facing two.
; Add eight to the actor's 16-bit X coordinate, preserving carry.
; At frame four, mark the actor retired in its flags and clear its active slot.
; Mark actor active, read its stage proximity parameter and use the common position window. Accepted activation enters state one and may spawn a reserved actor at its position.
; At frame two, set the retired flag and clear the active slot.
; Choose free reserved actor 1D or 1E, copy source coordinates and face toward the player. Initialize flags/state and request spawn audio; leave occupied slots unchanged.
; On animation-delay transitions, subtract a local vertical step and advance the bounded phase. After eight steps run the close-contact state transition, then continue horizontal terrain checks.
; Local bounded rise-step bytes used by the actor curve phase. Eight selected steps precede the neighboring behavior entry; remaining bounded constants retain their exact values.
; Check close contact, side and support probes. Choose a landing/turn state when obstructed, move down two pixels across an accepted step, or enter the shared hit reaction on a material collision.
; At the last delay tick, toggle left/right facing in the slot and actor record.
; Copy player coordinates and opposite facing into the actor. At later frames either apply periodic contact damage during player state 17 or enter the next actor state with a small Y shift.
; Copy all four position planes and choose the facing opposite the player in both actor and slot records.
; Advance a modulo-64 counter. On wrap apply two player damage; zero health enters the fixed life-loss flow.
; Pace a downward step by animation delay, test terrain/support, then align Y and enter state one on contact. Otherwise use the common side-probe direction reversal.
; Add A to the selected actor's 16-bit Y coordinate and return.
; Probe the facing-selected side with a ten-pixel offset; obstruction enters the shared direction reversal.
; Toggle actor/slot facing between two and four. Used by movement and pursuit behaviors after an obstructed probe.
; At a late animation phase, reject blockers and require a narrow player-relative position/facing window. Enter actor state four and nonlocally skip its caller's remaining movement.

; Require an eligible player facing opposite the actor inside a close window. Enter actor state six and player state 17, initialize a shared escape counter and retain controller state; rejection enters actor state five.
; Move actor down one pixel, probe support and side obstruction, and enter state eight with aligned Y and landing audio on contact.
; Temporarily map frame bank 12 to build both rectangles, restore the level bank and test overlap. On timeout reset actor behavior; on collision tail-dispatch the fixed hit response.
; Clear actor flags and its active slot when the animation reaches frame four.
; For an active actor, use the packed 88 proximity bound. Rejected actors are deactivated; accepted ones continue through the player-frame overlap test.
; Return when the actor is inactive.

; Unless player state 1D suppresses collection, build actor/player frame rectangles using bank 12 and restore the level bank before overlap testing. Acceptance enters collection state, adds 150 score units and requests sound.
; Hold a long animation delay, move down two pixels and probe support. Contact aligns Y, starts state two and a 70-tick retirement timer with landing audio.
; When the retirement timer expires, mark actor retired, clear its slot and update remaining/collected counters.
; Near the end of frame three, set the retired flag once and decrement the remaining count.
; Clear player state/frame/facing, set movement speed selector 2 and return.
; If the support probe succeeds, reset player frame, enter state four and choose movement speed two; otherwise return to idle.
; Enter state 0C with no movement facing, frame zero, delay eight and a transition sound.
